60.name: Astralis
60.headline: First LAN trophy since 2019, then a scramble

134.storyline: Aurora made the Cologne Major semi-finals, then rebuilt anyway. MAJ3R stepped down in July; Jimpphat and kyxsan joined XANTARES, Wicadia and woxic, with ash taking over as coach. The new five hit the podium fast: second at StarSeries Fall, third at ESL Pro League and the Thunderpick World Championship. Then Bucharest and Beijing cooled them off, and ash admits expectations "rose too quickly." Stage 3, Dec 2.

139.name: Falcons
139.headline: NiKo finally has his Major. Falcons want two
139.storyline: In Cologne, NiKo finally got his Major as Falcons beat FURIA in the final. karrigan, TeSeS, m0NESY and kyousuke make up the rest of the reigning champions. They haven't lifted a trophy since: an early BLAST Bounty exit, an Esports World Cup quarter-final loss to Legacy, then a FURIA defeat that ended their BLAST Rivals Season 2 run. The defence starts Dec 2, straight into Stage 3.

140.headline: M80 vs the top seed: best-of-one upset alert
140.storyline: Stage 2 has been M80's ceiling at each of the last three Majors, most recently a 1-3 exit in Cologne. 145.name: FUT
145.headline: World No.9 FUT need to rediscover April
145.storyline: In April, FUT were PGL Bucharest champions, 3-1 over Astralis with cmtry as MVP. By August they were in an Esports World Cup grand final, falling 1-3 to Spirit. Now the world No.9 arrive on a three-series skid, with coach coolio even standing in for a visa-hit Krabeni at BLAST Rivals. SunPayus starts in cmtry's place alongside xfl0ud, dem0n, Krabeni and dziugss. Top European seed in Stage 2, Nov 28.

149.headline: 1win become The One, and debut in Stage 2
149.storyline: Different name, same firepower. The One is the 1win roster, renamed because 1win isn't licensed to operate in Singapore.
